newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction forecast.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates climbed a sharp 140 basis points to close at 18.50 percent on Tuesday after market forecasts changed to predict imminent gains in primary rates, traders said.
"They're seeing the possibility of a turnaround in Cetes, which is why they were selling at those rates at the close," a trader said.

A Reuters survey revealed traders predicted Banco de Mexico would assign bellether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 18.19 percent. This would represent an increase of 12 basis points since last week's auction.
Individual predictions were divided, however, with forecasts ranging from gains of 50 basis points to falls of 25 basis points.
Dealers said secondary rates came under upside pressure from the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which was down 15/32 to yield 7.03 percent.
"The long bond is under pressure and hitting the (domestic) secondary market," a trader said.
Month-end demand for liquidity also heightened pressure on rates, traders said.

Despite apparent liquidity pressures, Banco de Mexico drained 3.880 billion pesos from the market, by assigning three direct Cetes sales and seven repurchase agreements. Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 40 basis points at 19.00 percent.
Cetes June futures contracts traded in Chicago closed down 27 basis points at 78.68 percent. Liquidity of 1.653 billion
pesos was due to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
